inventory: PiSharp model selection, thinking and configuration parity
phase: review correction implemented; paired differential complete; PR #24 draft with exact-head checks tracked in its description
classifications: supported with an intentional safety deviation
unsupported by the existing provider/platform boundary

features.feature: Exact, fuzzy, provider-qualified and ambiguous model references, including custom fallback and thinking suffixes
features.inputConfiguration: Optional provider constraint and model text; catalog models include provider, ID, name, reasoning and request metadata; provider usability comes from configured authentication or inline --api-key.
features.defaults: No model-reference default. Unknown explicit references may become custom model IDs for the selected provider.
features.precedence: Pinned Pi collects exact candidates, uses provider-prefix hints and authentication to resolve cross-provider ambiguity, then fuzzy candidates; valid thinking suffixes are considered after literal matching. PiSharp currently selects a provider before matching.
features.validation: Pinned strict CLI suffix parsing preserves invalid suffixes in the ID; lenient scope parsing warns and drops an invalid suffix. Exact matches are case-insensitive; fuzzy matches search IDs and names.
features.observableBehavior: Resolved provider/model, requested thinking, ambiguity candidates, warning/error text and fallback model identity.
features.providerRequestEffect: The resolved provider, endpoint, credential identity and model ID must drive the subsequent request.
features.persistence: Selection persistence is handled by model defaults or the session, not by reference parsing.
features.reloadBehavior: Re-resolution after catalog/auth refresh remains to be verified.
features.failureBehavior: Pinned ambiguity is explicit; an unavailable but unique match can still be selected for first-time authentication. PiSharp errors or falls back within a preselected provider.
features.knownDifference: 25 strict direct-Pi reference and CLI cases cover exact, qualified, fuzzy, ambiguous, authenticated-provider, suffix and error behavior.

features.feature: Fresh startup, saved defaults, explicit CLI choice, scoped-first choice, authentication fallback and session restoration
features.inputConfiguration: CLI provider/model/thinking, global and trusted-project defaults, enabledModels, available catalog/auth state and restored session metadata.
features.defaults: Pinned default thinking is medium; the first scoped model wins on a new session, followed by a configured default and then an available model. Exact fallback details depend on catalog/auth state.
features.precedence: Pinned source order is scoped model, saved default, then first available model; resume bypasses fresh scoped selection and restores session model state. PiSharp precedence is not yet differentially verified.
features.validation: Model capability constraints apply to the effective thinking level; missing providers/models and stale sessions have explicit recovery paths.
features.observableBehavior: Initial provider/model/thinking, fallback message, session metadata and next request.
features.providerRequestEffect: First request uses the effective startup or restored selection.
features.persistence: Saved default remains separate from transient session selection; session model/thinking are restored.
features.reloadBehavior: Catalog/auth changes and settings reload during startup remain to be verified.
features.failureBehavior: Unavailable saved/session model should recover without corrupting the session or silently rewriting defaults.
features.knownDifference: 10 strict direct-Pi cases cover fresh start, scope/default precedence, unauthenticated selection, empty catalogues, provider defaults and continuation behavior. RPC/session continuation retains a usable configured identity when no provider is authenticated; this existing-runtime adaptation is documented separately.

features.feature: Scoped model pattern resolution, ordering, diagnostics, duplicate elimination and per-pattern thinking
features.inputConfiguration: Ordered enabledModels or --models patterns matched against provider/model and bare model ID.
features.defaults: An empty scope means all configured models; first match order controls scoped ordering.
features.precedence: Pinned exact references are checked before glob interpretation; otherwise patterns are applied in order and models are deduplicated.
features.validation: Pinned uses minimatch with nocase; bracketed literal IDs are protected by exact lookup. Invalid thinking suffixes and no-match/ambiguity conditions produce diagnostics.
features.observableBehavior: Ordered scoped models and warning diagnostics; per-pattern thinking follows the selected scope entry.
features.providerRequestEffect: Scope constrains startup/cycling/picker choices but must not reroute an already active request.
features.persistence: Global or trusted-project enabledModels are persisted as ordered patterns.
features.reloadBehavior: Scope recomputation after settings/catalog reload remains to be verified.
features.failureBehavior: No-match and ambiguous patterns warn; malformed/oversized configuration is bounded by PiSharp validation.
features.knownDifference: 18 strict direct-Pi cases cover minimatch braces, ranges, extglobs, negation, escaped IDs, suffixes, ordering, ambiguity and diagnostics; the regex cache is bounded at 256 patterns.

features.feature: Interactive scope search, toggle, enable-all, clear, reorder, save, refresh and cancel
features.inputConfiguration: Current model catalog, ordered scope IDs/patterns, search text and selector actions.
features.defaults: Changes are session-only until the explicit save action; cancel leaves the prior scope unchanged.
features.precedence: Configured order is retained, newly enabled models follow the selector's defined order, and save writes the resulting scope.
features.validation: Unavailable configured IDs remain visible; refresh reconciles current catalog entries without silently losing saved choices.
features.observableBehavior: Search/toggle/bulk/reorder state, cancellation behavior and persisted order.
features.providerRequestEffect: Scope edits affect later model selection only.
features.persistence: Explicit save persists the scope; selector edits before save are transient.
features.reloadBehavior: Refresh and settings reload must retain valid user choices and handle unavailable entries.
features.failureBehavior: Cancel without mutation; save failures must not report success.
features.knownDifference: The interactive selector supports filtering, toggle, save and cancel while preserving unrelated settings. Native Windows/macOS PTY behavior was not exercised.
features.acceptanceStatus: implemented and verified on Linux PTY

features.feature: Thinking levels, suffix/default precedence, model compatibility and requested-versus-effective clamping
features.inputConfiguration: Requested CLI/suffix/session level, per-model default, global default, model reasoning capability and thinkingLevelMap.
features.defaults: PiSharp declares medium; pinned default and level support are sourced from agent-core and model metadata.
features.precedence: Explicit CLI, suffix, model override, global default and restored session values must be derived per startup/transition path.
features.validation: Seven levels are represented; model capability maps can remove or remap levels. Effective clamping must not silently rewrite saved preferences.
features.observableBehavior: Requested and effective level, selector choices, transition events and session restoration.
features.providerRequestEffect: Adapter-specific reasoning effort/mode/disable fields reflect effective thinking.
features.persistence: Per-model/global defaults persist; incidental clamping is not persisted unless source does so.
features.reloadBehavior: Model switch, resumed session and settings reload recompute effective thinking.
features.failureBehavior: Unsupported explicit values report or clamp according to the source path; transition failure must preserve the prior active state.
features.knownDifference: 10 strict direct-Pi cases cover scoped, per-model, global and current defaults, clamping, non-reasoning models and supported xhigh.

features.feature: Default/custom/per-level reasoning budgets, output-token room, clamping and provider compatibility
features.inputConfiguration: Effective level, configured budgets for minimal/low/medium/high, model/output token ceilings and provider compatibility metadata.
features.defaults: PiSharp currently uses 1024/2048/8192/16384 tokens and reserves 1024 answer tokens; exact provider-specific pinned defaults remain under review.
features.precedence: Provider mapper, model metadata, user budgets and requested output constraints must be compared per adapter.
features.validation: Non-negative integer budgets; clamp against output limits without overflow and omit unsupported fields.
features.observableBehavior: Effective request max output, reasoning budget and absent/present compatibility fields.
features.providerRequestEffect: Actual outgoing request body for supported token-budget and effort-based providers.
features.persistence: Configured budgets persist in user/project settings and project trust gates project values.
features.reloadBehavior: The next provider operation after settings reload uses the new budgets.
features.failureBehavior: Invalid settings do not partially alter active budgets; unsupported levels/fields are omitted or handled per source.
features.knownDifference: 10 strict option cases and provider-wire captures verify default/custom budgets, output ceilings and provider-specific omission/clamping.

features.feature: Model-level and thinking-level sampling parameters, max tokens, compatibility projection and switching
features.inputConfiguration: Provider/model catalog metadata, configured model overrides, samplingParams, samplingParamsByThinkingLevel, thinkingLevelMap and per-request options.
features.defaults: Provider/catalog metadata supplies model defaults; precedence and merge behavior are source-defined and not yet fully extracted.
features.precedence: Must verify model defaults, per-level values, explicit request overrides and provider compatibility adjustments from pinned mapper code.
features.validation: Invalid nested configuration must fail or be ignored exactly where source behavior specifies; unsupported fields must not leak.
features.observableBehavior: Actual resolved request options after model/provider/thinking transitions.
features.providerRequestEffect: Sampling fields in outgoing HTTP payload; absent fields are asserted too.
features.persistence: Catalog/configured model metadata is loaded from provider configuration; settings reload behavior remains to be verified.
features.reloadBehavior: Updated model metadata applies to subsequent requests without stale values.
features.failureBehavior: Malformed config fails safely and leaves the previous active runtime intact.
features.knownDifference: Model and per-thinking-level sampling merges are compared in the oracle and physical requests; provider-specific unsupported fields are omitted by the adapter.

features.feature: Model-related global/project/CLI/session settings, validation and project trust
features.inputConfiguration: Built-in defaults, user settings, trusted project settings, CLI flags, environment and restored session state for model/scope/thinking/budget fields.
features.defaults: Default thinking is medium; absent model/provider/scope values use runtime defaults.
features.precedence: PiSharp overlays project values over user values for selected fields and applies CLI defaults; pinned field-specific precedence still needs case-by-case verification.
features.validation: Typed JSON, duplicate-key checks, bounded file size/depth, valid thinking names, model keys and nonnegative budget integers.
features.observableBehavior: Effective value, origin/scope, validation diagnostic and whether project values are ignored while untrusted.
features.providerRequestEffect: Only effective trusted/explicit values reach provider configuration.
features.persistence: Settings are stored separately at user and project paths.
features.reloadBehavior: Trust changes and settings reload must recompute effective values without partial application.
features.failureBehavior: Malformed or untrusted project values must not redirect provider routing or credentials.
features.knownDifference: 10 strict direct-Pi cases cover global/project precedence, trust, defaults, model thinking, enabled-model order/removal and preservation of unrelated fields.

features.feature: Atomic settings changes, nested/model override updates, removal, coordinated concurrency, reload and restart
features.inputConfiguration: User/project settings JSON mutations, reload notifications and concurrent PiSharp writers.
features.defaults: Existing unrelated keys and nested values are preserved during an update.
features.precedence: Write then parse/validate, publish an effective settings snapshot, update relevant runtime owners and use it for the next operation.
features.validation: Malformed JSON, duplicate properties, BOM, invalid types, bounds, missing/empty/oversized files and write errors.
features.observableBehavior: On-disk JSON, active snapshot, next runtime value, restart value and failure atomicity.
features.providerRequestEffect: Subsequent requests use updated effective settings; invalid reload retains last valid state.
features.persistence: Atomic private-file writer and per-scope settings paths.
features.reloadBehavior: Live reload and restart are in scope; exact settings-to-runtime synchronization is unverified.
features.failureBehavior: No partial writes or partial active configuration; cancellation and write failures preserve valid state.
features.knownDifference: Settings writes are coordinated, atomically persisted and reloadable; deterministic concurrent updates and malformed-input handling are covered by the .NET suite.

features.feature: Model picker, scoped model editor, thinking selector, settings picker, search, cancellation and unsent draft preservation
features.inputConfiguration: Available catalog, current/default model, scope, supported thinking levels and effective settings scope.
features.defaults: Current selection is highlighted; default model/thinking values are labeled; cancellation does not change selection.
features.precedence: Selection and persistence actions follow pinned keybindings and selector callbacks; exact cross-surface behavior remains unverified.
features.validation: Only available models and model-supported thinking levels can be selected; settings edits validate before save.
features.observableBehavior: Search ranking, selected state, keyboard actions, focus/cursor/draft retention and save/cancel result.
features.providerRequestEffect: Committed selection changes affect subsequent requests only.
features.persistence: Model/default and settings save actions persist only when explicitly selected.
features.reloadBehavior: Catalog refresh while picker is open and settings live application remain to be verified.
features.failureBehavior: Cancellation or failed save leaves previous state active; no success event before commit.
features.knownDifference: Model/thinking selection and scoped-model editing have selector/PTY coverage. Native Windows/macOS interaction is not claimed.

features.feature: CLI model/provider/thinking/list/scope options and RPC model/thinking state transitions
features.inputConfiguration: --provider, --model, --thinking, --models, --list-models, --api-key, session flags and supported RPC operations.
features.defaults: Pinned flags and RPC operations are authoritative; PiSharp currently exposes a subset with custom semantics.
features.precedence: Explicit CLI and runtime transition behavior must agree where interfaces express the same action.
features.validation: Exact accepted values, exit codes, warnings/errors, cancellation and credential redaction.
features.observableBehavior: CLI output/exit status and RPC response/event/state after transition.
features.providerRequestEffect: The next request must match reported provider/model/thinking.
features.persistence: Only commands that explicitly save defaults/settings mutate persistent defaults; session selection persists per session.
features.reloadBehavior: RPC/TUI after reload must see the same effective catalog/settings snapshot.
features.failureBehavior: Blocked active runs, auth failures and cancellation cannot return false success or stale state.
features.knownDifference: 10 strict source-pinned CLI/TUI/RPC cases cover provider selection, suffixes, scoped model switching, clamping, errors and supported thinking levels.

features.feature: Session resume/replacement/fork/clone, persisted selection metadata and extension selection callbacks
features.inputConfiguration: Persisted session provider/model/thinking, current project runtime, transition source and extension registrations.
features.defaults: Restored session metadata applies unless explicit connection/model selection semantics override it.
features.precedence: Session selection, explicit CLI and saved defaults must match pinned per scenario.
features.validation: Restored provider/client/metadata must resolve as one valid runtime; failures preserve the prior state.
features.observableBehavior: JSONL/session state, extension event order/payload, active client and next provider request.
features.providerRequestEffect: First post-resume or post-transition call uses restored/committed identity.
features.persistence: Committed model/thinking transitions update session records; transient drafts and completed tool effects are preserved.
features.reloadBehavior: Session replacement and project runtime adoption remain to be verified under catalog/settings changes.
features.failureBehavior: No duplicate callback, tool replay, stale runtime or success event on failed transition.
features.knownDifference: Fresh start, model/thinking changes, extension selection events, replacement and resume are covered by process tests. Extended busy-run transition interleavings are not represented in the direct oracle.
features.acceptanceStatus: implemented and verified by process regressions

features.feature: Physical provider request effects of model, thinking, budget, sampling, reload and session changes
features.inputConfiguration: Resolved model and provider, effective thinking/budget/sampling, messages/tools and local fixture credentials.
features.defaults: Adapter and model metadata defaults; no live provider credentials are needed.
features.precedence: Per-adapter serialization is authoritative; no universal reasoning field is assumed.
features.validation: Assert present and absent wire fields, provider routing and credential identity.
features.observableBehavior: Captured local HTTP method/path/headers/body and resulting provider response handling.
features.providerRequestEffect: Direct physical request comparison for supported OpenAI Responses/Chat, Anthropic Messages and token-budget-capable paths; Google adapters where supported.
features.persistence: Not persisted by the HTTP layer; derives from effective runtime/configuration.
features.reloadBehavior: Updated configuration must affect the next captured request.
features.failureBehavior: Auth/provider changes cannot leak credentials across providers or leave stale parameters.
features.knownDifference: 23 direct pinned-Pi local-HTTP cases cover OpenAI Responses/Completions, Anthropic Messages, Google Generative AI and Vertex request fields, credentials, budgets and sampling.

features.feature: Reproducible direct-Pi oracle, independent calibration and minimum 80 meaningful cases with provenance
features.inputConfiguration: Synthetic models/auth/settings and temporary workspaces; local HTTP endpoints for provider-wire cases.
features.defaults: Every case records the pinned SHA and actual PiSharp SHA; no expected output is generated from PiSharp.
features.precedence: Direct pinned source/process is the expected result; same-Pi control is independently repeated.
features.validation: Case provenance includes platform, oracle, input, auth/config, invocation, comparison policy, classification and result.
features.observableBehavior: Case-level strict pass/fail, category counts, calibration and exclusions.
features.providerRequestEffect: Wire cases capture actual HTTP payloads and headers.
features.persistence: Case workspaces are isolated; machine-readable reports are committed as compact reviewed evidence.
features.failureBehavior: Retain failed calibrations and real differences; normalization cannot hide provider/model/thinking/settings divergences.
features.knownDifference: The direct Pi oracle has 93 strict behavior cases; separate provider-wire evidence has 35 strict cases. Reports include pinned Pi and PiSharp SHAs, platform, inputs, auth/configuration, comparison policy and results.

features.feature: Concurrent settings/model transitions, reload, refresh, cancellation, large inputs and failure recovery
features.inputConfiguration: Deterministic barriers for concurrent writers, active provider/tool runs, refresh/reload and malformed or large inputs.
features.defaults: No arbitrary timeout is used to hide deadlocks; work and memory remain bounded.
features.precedence: A transition publishes only after preparation and commit; the last valid config remains active after invalid reload.
features.validation: Thousands of models, long IDs, many patterns, large settings files within the configured limit and malformed nested JSON.
features.observableBehavior: No lost updates, stale clients/budgets/sampling, duplicate events, replayed tool effects, deadlocks or secret leakage.
features.providerRequestEffect: Requests before/after barriers retain the correct provider/model/config snapshot.
features.persistence: Concurrent PiSharp updates are coordinated; arbitrary external writers are not assumed to share that lock.
features.reloadBehavior: Reload during model selection must publish an atomic effective snapshot.
features.failureBehavior: Cancellation/failure leaves previous valid runtime/settings usable and avoids partial success.
features.knownDifference: The suite covers 2,048-model catalogues, 96 scope patterns, bounded matching/cache behavior, concurrent settings mutation and failure/reload paths. Busy-run interleavings beyond existing process coverage remain a limitation.
